newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-FEYENOORD FUME OVER SPONSORSHIP ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FEYENOORD FUME OVER SPONSORSHIP ROW.

text.p: Dutch soccer league leaders Feyenoord are threatening legal action against U.S. sportswear firm Reebok International over the breakdown of a 25 million guilder ($14.65 million) sponsorship deal, Dutch media reported on Thursday.
Feyenoord directors are quoted as saying that Reebok reneged on a five-year deal, due to start next summer, to sponsor the Rotterdam club.

Reebok was quoted as saying the December 1995 "deal" was only an agreement in principle and Feyenoord, who regarded it as final, baulked at Reebok's insertion of an opt-out clause should Feyenoord's notorious fans "seriously misbehave", daily Volkskrant said.

Reebok was also said to have pulled out because Feyenoord's amateur team was going to continue to wear shirts emblazoned with the Adidas logo, one of Reebok's main rivals and Feyenoord's current sponsors.
Feyenoord director Nicole Edelenbos told the ANP news agency she wanted a swift resolution.
"Otherwise we'll take legal action. We're not happy having to do that, but we will if we have to."
